rationale: Neuroimaging findings across all documented PLAA-associated cohorts in the provided literature (Hall et al. 2017, Falik Zaccai et al. 2017, Chitre et al. 2018, and Dehghani et al. 2021) consistently identify a thin corpus callosum or progressive thinning of the corpus callosum alongside cerebellar/cerebral atrophy and delayed myelination, rather than primary callosal agenesis. No counter-examples reporting complete agenesis of the corpus callosum or preserved normal callosal morphology post-infancy in PLAA-deficient individuals were identified in the corpus.

evidence.text: Neuroimaging in affected individuals harboring PLAA variants in the first year of life demonstrated significant volume reduction and thinning of the corpus callosum accompanying progressive microcephaly and cerebellar volume reduction.
